figure.name: Ludwig von Mises
figure.era: Austrian School, calculation debate, and anti-interventionism (1920-1973)
figure.role: Austrian School economist known for the economic calculation problem, defense of markets, criticism of socialism, and influence on libertarian and free-market thought.
figure.hook: Mises = prices, private property, calculation, and the Austrian critique of socialism.
whyHere: Mises belongs here because capitalism's intellectual defense includes a hard claim about knowledge, prices, private property, and economic calculation.
He matters because his critique of socialism is not only moral; it argues that complex economies need market prices to compare alternatives.
figure.cleanIdea: Mises argues that without private property in the means of production and market prices, planners cannot rationally calculate complex economic choices.

figure.discussionText: This is the planned debate room for Mises: Austrian economics, prices, calculation, interventionism, private property, socialism, and whether markets solve coordination better than planners.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: The Austrian critique says socialism faces a price-and-calculation problem when planners replace private property and market exchange.

ideas.title: Austrian Economics
ideas.plainDefinition: Austrian economics is a market-oriented school emphasizing individual action, prices, entrepreneurship, time, knowledge, and limits on central planning.
ideas.context: In the Mises path, Austrian economics is the framework behind the calculation critique.
ideas.whyMatters: Austrian economics matters because it gives capitalism a theory of markets as discovery and coordination, not just buying and selling.

ideas.title: Economic Calculation
ideas.plainDefinition: Economic calculation is the use of prices, costs, profits, losses, and accounting to compare possible uses of scarce resources.
ideas.context: In the Mises path, economic calculation is the central problem he says socialism cannot solve without market prices.
ideas.whyMatters: Economic calculation matters because any serious political economy has to explain how choices are compared when resources are limited.

ideas.title: Interventionism
ideas.plainDefinition: Interventionism is government action that changes market outcomes through controls, subsidies, mandates, protections, taxes, or regulations.
ideas.context: In the Mises path, interventionism is treated as a distortion of market coordination.
ideas.whyMatters: Interventionism matters because capitalist thinkers disagree sharply over when public rules correct markets and when they break them.
